A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same 4DMoT/MV-DiT research, renamed from MTVCrafter to MTVCraft. Both provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Changes in experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons but do not prevent reliable assessment of the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original TikTok results and ablations in Tables 1–2, qualitative animation experiments, and appendix analyses of codebook usage and gymnastics reconstruction.

after.justification: v5 reports original 6B/18B results on TikTok and Fashion, component ablations in Tables 2 and 4, and additional qualitative and model-scaling experiments.

M1.justification: v5 changes the motion representation from normalized joints using estimated body shapes to neutral-shape, first-frame-relative coordinates with root translation. Motion attention changes from every CogVideoX block to every second block, and vision queries receive 4D positional encoding. The new Wan-based 18B variant adds text/image conditioning, zero-padded motion embeddings, and masked reference latents (Sections 3.1–3.3; Appendices A and C).

E1.justification: v5 adds Fashion as an evaluated benchmark, whereas v1 only cites it. It also evaluates motion transfer to non-humanoid subjects such as birds, a chair, and a fire hydrant (Figures 1, 14, and 16), extending v1's predominantly real and stylized humanoid examples. Gymnastics reconstruction and earlier human galleries are retained.

E2.justification: The TikTok comparison in Table 1 substantially changes membership. Animate-X, RealisDance-DiT, and UniAnimate-DiT are added, while MRAA, DreamPose, MagicAnimate, Champ, and Human-DiT disappear from that table. MimicMotion and ControlNeXt remain. Several older comparators remain in qualitative figures, so they have not been removed from the entire paper.

E3.justification: The reported training corpus increases from 5K to 30K pairs. DiT training changes from 20K to 30K iterations, the learning rate from 1e-5 to 2e-5, fixed 49-frame clips to variable 33–129-frame sampling, and motion-condition dropout from 0.25 to 0.2. v5 evaluates 6B/18B configurations and specifies text conditioning. Evaluation is now described by reference to RealisDance-DiT without restating v1's explicit TikTok split and crop.

E4.justification: v5 adds differential-motion, 3D-quantization, and 2D-spatial-RoPE ablations, extends component testing to Fashion, and reports unsuccessful linear/MLP adapters and pretrained SMPL-parameter tokenization for the 18B model (Appendix H). Codebook, gymnastics, attention-map, and CFG analyses already existed in v1. The earlier visual component-ablation grid and extreme-proportions failure panel are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark results. The codebook-frequency analysis is retained. Pose-estimation uncertainty filtering concerns dataset curation and does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting for the experimental findings.

E6.justification: TikTok and ablation values are substantially replaced: v1 reports FVD/FID-VID of 140.60/6.98, while v5 reports 317.21/8.56 for 6B and 276.65/7.31 for 18B. These use revised models and settings and do not establish a same-setting gain or loss. v5 adds Fashion results, non-humanoid animation outcomes, and negative findings from 18B design experiments.

T1.justification: Local mathematical definitions change: motion M becomes first-frame-relative, vision-query positional encoding changes from 3D to 4D, and Appendix C defines the new zero-padded reference and masked input latents. The VQ loss and motion-RoPE algorithm remain essentially unchanged. No new theorems or proofs appear; Appendix J mainly explains existing evaluation metrics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the contribution from human animation to arbitrary-character animation explicitly including animals and objects, and add scalability across CogVideoX and Wan backbones. The benchmark claim expands from TikTok to TikTok and Fashion, while v1's specific 6.98 FID-VID and 65% advantage claim disappears. The central direct-4D-tokenization novelty claim remains.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive explanations for neutral-shape and differential coordinates, their advantages over SMPL parameters, and the roles of motion representation and backbone capacity in generalization. v1's specific extreme-proportions/non-human-anatomy limitation becomes a general dependence on base-model capability in v5 Appendix D. Hand-control limitations and the inability to animate multiple people with independent poses remain.

D1.justification: v5 documents numerical precision, DeepSpeed ZeRO-2, warm-up, augmentations, a 55-degree pose-estimation camera setting, and the 18B model's frozen/trainable components. Appendix J adds metric implementation details. Access information changes from an anonymous code link to a named project and commercial service. Conversely, v1's explicit TikTok sequence IDs, 512×512 evaluation crop, and approximately 90-second inference time are omitted.

R1.justification: Related work is updated with AnimateDiff, UniAnimate-DiT, HyperMotion, RealisDance-DiT, Wan, and Wan-Animate, among others. v5 also makes the distinction between joint-coordinate and SMPL-parameter tokenization more explicit. The central research positioning against rendered 2D pose guidance remains intact, making this an update rather than a wholesale repositioning.

P1.justification: v5 substantially rewrites method explanations and reorganizes the narrative around arbitrary characters and model scaling. It removes the latent-diffusion primer, subdivides implementation and tokenizer/RoPE discussions, separates qualitative comparisons from visualization appendices, and moves CFG analysis out of the main text. The title, terminology, authorship, and conference presentation also change.

P2.justification: The teaser is expanded, the 6B architecture diagram is revised, and an 18B schematic is added. TikTok tables are restructured and Fashion comparison/ablation tables are introduced. Qualitative comparisons are replaced or rearranged, new galleries are added, and the CFG plot moves to the appendix. The component-ablation grid and one failure panel disappear; captions, page layout, and appendix navigation are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens validation through Fashion evaluation, newer DiT comparisons, and ablations isolating depth and differential-motion contributions. The second-backbone implementation and expanded technical documentation also make applicability more assessable. These gains address v1's narrower empirical support. Tradeoffs remain: explicit local evaluation details are lost, uncertainty is still unreported, and the Fashion claim of superiority across all metrics conflicts with Table 3's LPIPS ranking (RealisDance-DiT 0.053 versus MTVCraft-18B 0.057). These weaknesses temper but do not outweigh the stronger empirical and technical support.
